reading.body:
Alan Turing's two most consequential contributions are distinct and should not be collapsed: the 1936 paper made universal computation mathematically possible, and the 1950 paper made machine intelligence a scientific question worth pursuing.

The 1936 work defined the abstract machine that every physical computer still instantiates. Without that theoretical foundation there is no architecture to build, no chip to fabricate, no data center to power. The 1950 paper then asked whether a machine running on that architecture could exhibit intelligence, and proposed an operational test rather than a philosophical one. That move transformed AI from speculation into a research program with a measurable target.

What the data does not cover is the path from these ideas to physical hardware, energy consumption, or scale. Turing worked in mathematics and logic, not in buildings or grids. The connection to compute infrastructure is real but indirect: his theoretical model is the ancestor of every processor that now drives AI workloads, but the data here stops at the intellectual origin and does not trace that descent. His life ended in 1954, two years after the state he had served prosecuted him, and decades before the scaling dynamics this site tracks came into view.

standing.watch: The records contain no pending case, no planned listing and no dispute involving this person. Nothing in the profile or quick facts points to an unresolved matter, and the five news stories are dated items about manufacturing AI, sovereign compute and defense manufacturing that do not name him in their substance. The only forward-looking material is those 2026 stories themselves, and they do not concern him directly. Where the records are this thin, the honest reading is that there is nothing to watch beyond the continued use of his name on computing's highest award and on the universal machine model every computer still follows.
standing.record: The site's record for this person is a profile, a set of quick facts and five news stories listed as naming him. The quick facts cover the universal computing machine of 1936, Hut 8 at Bletchley Park, the imitation game now called the Turing Test, and the Turing Award. The five stories, dated from August to October 2026, concern manufacturing AI transformation, sovereign AI compute, advanced defense manufacturing, citizen-centric manufacturing for MSMEs, and an Ulsan forum on manufacturing and everyday AI. None of those stories describes Turing, his papers or his wartime work, and none reports a company, case or dispute involving him. The pattern is that the coverage carrying his name is contemporary industrial and manufacturing AI news, while the biographical material sits entirely in the profile and quick facts.
standing.standing: Alan Turing stands in these records as the father of theoretical computer science and artificial intelligence, the person who supplied both of AI's founding documents. The 1936 paper proved that one universal machine could compute anything computable, and the 1950 paper asked whether machines can think. The first made computers possible, and the second made artificial intelligence a research question rather than a fantasy. He led the Hut 8 team at Bletchley Park that broke German naval Enigma in the Second World War. Computing's highest honor, the Turing Award, bears his name. The records show no company he controls, no current role and no holdings, so his standing here is historical and foundational rather than operational.

achievements.title: On Computable Numbers (1936)
achievements.impact: Introduced the Turing machine and universal computation, the theoretical basis of every computer built since.

achievements.title: Breaking naval Enigma at Bletchley Park (1939-1945)
achievements.impact: The bombe machines and Banburismus methods he devised shortened the Atlantic war; historians credit the effort with saving vast numbers of lives.

achievements.title: Computing Machinery and Intelligence (1950)
achievements.impact: Reframed 'can machines think?' as an operational test, predicted machine learning, and answered Lovelace's objection, the founding paper of AI.

achievements.title: The chemical basis of morphogenesis (1952)
achievements.impact: Founded mathematical biology with reaction-diffusion theory, showing his computational lens reached beyond machines.
